page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an ARM64-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 2.6 GHz, with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 474 GB of local NVMe SSD storage as instance store volumes and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute workloads. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, along with Geekbench software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing, all fall within the middle 50% tier. However, certain workloads reveal performance tradeoffs. While Passmark memory scores are strong, placing in the top 25%, Passmark CPU scores and encryption tests are weak, landing in the bottom 25%. Similarly, single-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor, falling into the bottom 10%, and multi-threaded decompression is weak. Large-model LLM inference prompt processing is also limited, though text generation speeds for small and medium models remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m7gd.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density by combining dedicated ARM64 cores with integrated local NVMe SSD storage. This eliminates the need for separate network-attached storage for temporary data, optimizing the hardware-to-resource profile. The instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, database operations, and caching applications like Redis, where its strong memory performance and local NVMe storage can be leveraged.
